facts.fact: The Nigeria Data Protection Commission, led by National Commissioner and CEO Vincent Olatunji, released its annual report and said it investigated 213 cases under the Nigeria Data Protection Act in 2024.

NGA.note: No ruling against a named organisation or count of settled decisions by the commission is stated; the Meta fine is attributed to the government under consumer and data protection laws, not to the commission.

facts.fact: The article says the Nigeria Data Protection Act was enacted in 2023, strengthening the 2019 Regulations with provisions on lawful processing, consent, security and penalties.
The Nigeria Data Protection Commission, headed by National Commissioner and CEO Vincent Olatunji, was enforcing the Act in 2024-2025.

The commission says it investigated 213 privacy breaches, unauthorised data sharing and non-compliance cases under the Act in 2024, received 4,691 compliance audit returns for 2023-2024 and verified 2,888 data protection officers.
The Nigeria Data Protection Commission, with National Commissioner and CEO Vincent Olatunji, is acting as the country's data protection body.
The commission reports 4,691 compliance audit returns for 2023-2024, 2,888 verified data protection officers and 213 investigations in 2024.
The commissioner said the commission is strengthening its participation in the Network of African Data Protection Authorities.
